promptRaw:
"this is the style guide for my game: STYLE GUIDE — Year 2200 Isometric Architecture

Unified interior and architectural design language built from cold, perfect white mineral surfaces resembling carved Greek white sandstone or dense architectural ceramic. Forms are monolithic, heavy, and rectilinear, appearing carved from a single solid mass rather than assembled from parts. Edges are sharp with minimal chamfering; rounded corners are rare and structural, never decorative. Surfaces are pristine, new, and well-maintained — no damage, decay, grime, or chaos. Exterior aging, if present, is subtle and passive.

The setting is the year 2200. Civilization functions but is depopulated due to low birth rates, not war. Spaces are calm, sterile, melancholic, intentional, and designed — never cozy, never ruined, never heroic.

Visual language follows a strict architectural system:

Fixed square modular grid.

Infrastructure-first logic (walls, doors, windows are structural, not props).

Corners are solid, dedicated volumes.

No clutter, no ornamental detailing.

Low-to-mid mesh detail with strong, readable silhouettes.

Accent system:

Single accent color only: burnt industrial amber (#B8430E).

Used sparingly and functionally.

Often appears as a clean horizontal stripe at a consistent architectural datum.

Indicators and controls use the same amber.

No additional accent colors.

Windows:

Narrow, vertical, very dark tinted — near-black voids.

Read as absence rather than transparency.

Technology:

High-end but understated and slightly obsolete.

Physical interaction preferred over screens.

Buttons and controls are rare, grouped, recessed, and intentional.

Screens are minimal, secondary, or inactive.

Lighting:

Neutral, even, non-dramatic.

Optimized for gameplay readability.

No cinematic contrast or exaggerated glow.

Rendering style:

Classic isometric view with orthographic feel.

Fallout 1–2 inspired proportions.

Clean topology.

No micro-detailing.

No decorative bevels.

No texture clutter.

Atmosphere:
Calm, sterile, structured, slightly melancholic, depopulated but functioning civilization — a designed future, not a broken one.

 professional workbench chair 3/4 view, product shot, centered object, plain mid-gray background."
